methodology: Five-ayah preliminary comparative screening based on known narrative outlines. Critical primary editions, exact wording, witnesses and stable source URLs not independently checked; Exodus leads are for future collation only, not public verified parallels. Reviewed previous open PR #267 (7:116–120) and PR #93 security warning; avoid duplicate counting. No claim of borrowing.

records.notes: Qur'an reports a declaration of faith by Pharaoh's magicians after the contest. Exodus 8:19 has magicians acknowledge divine power during the later plague of gnats, not a conversion or proclamation of belief.
records.pending_question: Check Hebrew and Greek textual forms and distinguish different narrative moments; search pre-Islamic retellings for explicit conversion.

records.topic: They affirm the Lord of Moses and Aaron
records.notes: The Qur'anic declaration names Moses and Aaron's Lord. Exodus 8:19 says 'finger of God' in a later scene; it does not narrate this confession by the magicians.
records.pending_question: Check exact divine-name language and pre-Islamic witness to magicians' confession without conflating scenes.

records.topic: Pharaoh accuses magicians of believing without permission and alleges conspiracy
records.notes: Exodus presents Pharaoh resisting Moses but not this accusation of unauthorized belief and conspiracy by his magicians.
records.pending_question: Seek securely dated Jewish, Syriac or Christian expansions; do not treat general Pharaoh resistance as an individual-verse parallel.

records.notes: The threat of cutting opposite hands and feet and crucifixion is distinctive in this Qur'anic scene; cited Exodus episodes involve oppression or magicians' inability, not this punishment.
records.pending_question: Investigate pre-Islamic attestations of cross-amputation and crucifixion separately from an alleged Moses-era event; do not infer historicity or date from motif alone.

records.topic: Magicians say they will return to their Lord
records.notes: The Qur'an records the magicians' response to Pharaoh's threat. Exodus lacks this exchange; acknowledgement of God's power at Exodus 8:19 is not an equivalent speech.
records.pending_question: Check securely pre-Islamic narrative witnesses and avoid treating a general martyrdom motif as a textual parallel.

pending_questions: Collate Exodus 7–9 in MT and LXX with precise edition and manuscript dates; do not merge different scenes.
Investigate pre-Islamic Jewish and Syriac witnesses for magicians' conversion, punishment and response.
Reconcile open screening PRs into one authoritative ledger.
